change: a lab or quiz that some class has closed is no longer served to a request with no token, so signing out or opening incognito stops being a way past a teacher's lock
_context: The gate has always answered 'is this open for MY class'. A request with no token has no class, so resolveGate returned self-study and the item was served in full. The teacher who reported the original lab bug found this by checking her own fix in incognito. Measured against production the same day: all 7 authored labs, and an AP Cyber Unit 1 quiz, were served complete to an anonymous request with locked absent or false.
_the_rule_and_why_it_is_narrow: Refusing anonymous OUTRIGHT would close the bypass and take the public practice layer offline, which CLAUDE.md calls a strategic loss rather than a security win. So only an item carrying an explicit CLOSING gate row for at least one class is withheld; an item nobody has closed is still served to anyone and still indexable. The rule reads gate ROWS ONLY and never a class default, because a class switched to locked-by-default has expressed a posture about its own students, not a judgement that every quiz on the site should leave the public index.
_two_bugs_this_found_in_its_own_implemen: First, the anonymous path asked about each lab alias in turn and refused on the first close, which ignored an explicit reopen on the other name. Second, and only found by the generated rederive, a TIE between two same-scope rows was broken by alias order: a teacher closing the Lab column while a stale terminal-lab row sat open would have watched their click do nothing, which is the exact complaint that started this thread. A tie now goes to the CLOSING row, in both the anonymous and the signed-in path, so there is one opinion about precedence rather than two that agreed by luck.
_live_note: verify-anon-gate-live.js reads live state it does not control. If no teacher has anything closed at the moment it runs, there is nothing for the rule to refuse and the script says UNPROVEN rather than passing. Its four assertions are therefore a GUARD, not the proof: they fail if the public practice layer goes dark, if a refusal does not name the anonymous rule, or if a refused lab puts its spec on the wire anyway. The rederive kind carries the positive evidence here, which is why it is present.
_expect_failure_note: Every expect_failure carries the literal [FAIL] prefix, because an assertion NAME appears on the pass line too and would prove only that it ran.
